page.layout: One printed page. Running head centred at top. One text block of roman type with a Greek and Latin phrase. Below the last full line, one line in smaller italic type with Greek. Catchword "Sed" at the lower right.

main_text.p: De iurisprudentia & medicina idem est iudicium. Sed quid ego iu-uentutem commemoro? Senes philosophi, iurisconsulti & medici portum suae sapientiae constituunt sacram Scripturam. Quin itaque imitamur Alexandrum Magnum, qui tanto erga Homeri Iliada flagrauit amore, ut illam velut ἐφόδιον τῆς ἀρετῆς[?] in castris circumferre, noctuque loco puluinaris capiti suo substernere sit solitus: & Platonem, qui Sophronem suum noctu sub culcitra collocauit, & iam moribundus capiti suo subiectum habuit: deniq; Scipionem Africanum, qui Xenophontem de παιδείας[?] Cyri nunquam e manibus depofuit. Hos, inquam, ethnicos cur non imitamur in sanctiore & utiliore studio, lectione nimirum Scripturae sacrae, quae sola est

p.i: κειμήλιον αἰώνιον, πηγὴ χρυσοφόρος[?], θη-σαυρὸς ἀμίαντος, Φάρμακον ψυχῆς, βίου ἐπιστήμης.

page.notes: The first paragraph of the page is set in roman type with italic words. The Greek words in the body ("ἐφόδιον τῆς ἀρετῆς", "παιδείας") are small and hard to read at this scan size; those readings are guesses and are marked [?]. The footer Greek line is also partly illegible and only its clearer parts are copied. "lectione" appears as "le" at the line end followed by "ctione"; the hyphen is not clearly printed, so it is written whole. Long s has been rendered as plain s throughout. The printed "depofuit" is kept as printed.
